About this initiative

The Thought Leaders series aims to provide a platform for the brightest minds in the social sciences and humanities to share their reflections on major societal issues and propose innovative ideas for addressing them.

Through these discussions, we seek to inspire and empower policymakers, academics, and citizens to question and redefine societal paradigms, approaching global challenges from fresh perspectives. The Thought Leaders series contributes to the recent mandate of the Management of Social Transformations (MOST) Programme to support decision-makers in reassessing socioeconomic paradigms.

Speakers include scientists, philosophers, climate activists, academics, writers, and political decision-makers. 

Thought Leader: Lê Nguyên Hoàng

Lê Nguyên Hoang holds a PhD in mathematics and is a former professor at the University of Lausanne. His research focuses on developing artificial intelligence and AI governance systems grounded in democratic principles. He is also a widely recognized science communicator, with more than 20 million views on YouTube, and the author of seven books.

His publications include The Dictatorship of Algorithms (2024), which warns about the risks posed by recommendation algorithms rather than generative artificial intelligence, and Le fabuleux chantier (2019), which underscores the urgency of designing robustly beneficial AI and sets out concrete pathways for developing safer algorithms aligned with the public interest.

He is currently the Executive Director of Tournesol, a nonprofit organization behind Tournesol.app, a platform dedicated to researching digital democracy solutions and advocating for a safer online environment.

Governing AI today: Priorities for Inclusive and Resilient Societies

This lecture will explore the design, deployment, and societal consequences of contemporary AI systems. It will highlight the ways in which these technologies can produce harmful effects on healthcare, democratic processes, and the spread of hatred, while emphasizing the urgent need for thoughtful governance.

The speaker will examine approaches to AI oversight that aim to mitigate risks, protect vulnerable populations, and strengthen democratic institutions. Key themes will include addressing conflicts of interest in AI development, promoting functional interoperability, and reinforcing the democratic foundations of cyberspace—such as transparency, security, informed judgment, and shared access to information.

By combining technical insight with governance perspectives, the lecture will offer a roadmap for developing AI systems that are aligned with public interest and social responsibility.

 

UNESCO and the “la Caixa” Foundation

This Thought Leaders Lecture is part of the joint programme of conferences and events organised by UNESCO’s MOST Programme in partnership with the “la Caixa” Foundation.

The ongoing collaboration between MOST and “la Caixa” reinforces UNESCO’s role as a laboratory of ideas supporting evidence-informed policymaking. This intellectual partnership provides a platform for policy dialogue and knowledge exchange in the social and human sciences, helping to strengthen capacities for more inclusive, equitable, and sustainable public policies.
